findings: 'Activity' nav destination /dashboard/activity (navConfig.js) renders NO surface — falls through to PlaceholderPage; #708 added only explanatory copy. This is the unbuilt cross-domain destination UX-3 concerns.
Control Tower 'Activity Timeline' panel — global/system-wide, jobs-derived via buildTimeline(jobs) over all fieldops_jobs. Derived-only, not persisted.
'Operational History' (WorkOrderDetail) — same buildTimeline builder scoped to ONE work order (jobsForWorkOrder). Not a competing authority — a narrower view of #2.
Dispatcher Board 'Recent Activity (this session)' — global WO status changes, session-scoped + ephemeral (in-memory, max 50, gone on reload). Distinct data source (useSessionActivityFeed).
Account 'Service Activity' / 'Account Activity' — single Account's Work Orders queried from fieldops_wos (third data source).

Wayfinding discrepancy: the /dashboard/activity placeholder says the live timeline is in 'Service Operations', but the panel actually lives in Control Tower; no screen is labeled 'Service Operations'.
Term collision: 'Activity' names four different things at four grains, backed by three different data sources.

evidence.note: read-only repo tracing, 22 tool uses, no browser

questionsRaised: What is the intended data grain of a standalone /dashboard/activity destination (global vs per-technician vs 'my activity' vs cross-domain roll-up)?
Does a standalone Activity destination duplicate the already-live Control Tower Activity Timeline (if global)?
Should the placeholder wayfinding text be corrected to name an actual surface (Control Tower)?
How should the four 'Activity'-named surfaces be disambiguated for users given differing scope and persistence?
